cartography.label: Continental organization
cartography.explanation: Choose coherent continental interiors or dispersed crust assemblies. Ocean coverage is independent; motion and the water budget determine which landmasses remain separate.

cartography.label: Ocean coverage
cartography.explanation: Set the initial exposed land share without changing the amount or organization of continental crust. Later history changes the shores.

cartography.label: Continental motion
cartography.explanation: Set how strongly plates move and rework continents through history. Motion changes coasts, opens or closes seas and builds new collision ranges independently of inherited terrain.

cartography.label: Terrain
cartography.explanation: Choose inherited mountain relief and how erosion, deposition and glaciers rework it. Continental motion, shoreline detail and island organization have separate controls.

cartography.label: Distinctive landmarks
cartography.explanation: The prominence of volcanic districts and crater landforms. Footprints scale with the map, and history determines what survives.

cartography.label: Shoreline
cartography.explanation: Broad reworked outlines, intricate inlets, or deposited river-mouth lowlands. Sediment supply and coastal exposure still matter.

cartography.label: Climate coverage
cartography.explanation: The latitude zones represented by this map, independent of its dimensions and map boundary.

cartography.label: Warmth
cartography.explanation: Shift snowlines and growing conditions. Latitude, altitude, sea transport and magical heat determine local temperatures.

cartography.label: Living landscape
cartography.explanation: Vegetation, seasonal stress, fire and browsing respond together to water and climate. Isolated or recently disturbed ground still needs time to recover.

cartography.label: Core-site prevalence
cartography.explanation: Core-site prevalence scales with land area; geothermal peaks and physical spacing determine which sites can form.

cartography.label: Thermal reach
cartography.explanation: How far heat follows connected conductive veins from core sites.

cartography.label: Heat and quickening
cartography.explanation: Thermal warming, ice melt, quickened life and fire exposure from the same Fire field.

cartography.label: Hardened terrain
cartography.explanation: Heat-baked rock resists erosion and retains its landform imprint.

cartography.label: Charge-bearing terrain
cartography.explanation: Cold and elevated terrain supplies charge to the coldward network.

cartography.label: Ice-capture pattern
cartography.explanation: Concentration in ice reservoirs versus continued transport toward colder ground.

cartography.label: Softened terrain
cartography.explanation: Aurora weakens rock, changing its response to weathering and erosion.

cartography.label: Ocean influence extent
cartography.explanation: The reach and width of Pressure paths through connected ocean, coastal impulses and wakes.

cartography.label: Moved water
cartography.explanation: Upwelling, cold sea surface and fog where a front shoals; warm still water in its wakes.

cartography.label: Coastal stress
cartography.explanation: Additional coastal force where Pressure reaches the shore, combined with local waves and currents.

cartography.label: Ancient wake prevalence
cartography.explanation: The prevalence of historical wake paths scales with ocean area; their travel distances follow map scale.

cartography.label: Rogue-impact prevalence
cartography.explanation: The prevalence of Pressure-driven coastal impulses scales with shoreline length in the geographic history.

cartography.label: Stillness
cartography.explanation: How far charged ice outlasts its climate and slows the life within it.

cartography.label: Old-growth threshold
cartography.explanation: How old and how closed a canopy, or how deep a peat, must be before it is a stand.

cartography.label: Reach between roots
cartography.explanation: How far Greenwood travels through connected living cover from its stands and springs.

cartography.label: Verdure
cartography.explanation: Forest past its climate, deeper soil and braided rivers from the same Greenwood field.

cartography.label: Brine seep
cartography.explanation: How far brine travels down the drainage before the air flushes it or a pit crusts it.

cartography.label: Salt dust
cartography.explanation: How much of an exposed bed the wind lifts and how far it blows before it settles.

cartography.label: Glass flats and drying
cartography.explanation: How deep a bed fuses the pan to glass, and how much the air dries over salted ground.

cartography.label: Sanctuary reach
cartography.explanation: How wide a ring a long-kept seat wards, and how long a seat must be kept to ward one.

cartography.label: Kept lines and pilgrim roads
cartography.explanation: How many kept years make a frontier a ward line, and how worn a way must be to be a pilgrimage road.

cartography.label: Warding
cartography.explanation: How much of every other system a ring removes inside and lays on its rim, and how hard the rock holds within.

cartography.label: Tearing
cartography.explanation: How much strain between systems tears the ground, and how much makes a full tear.

cartography.label: Doors
cartography.explanation: How strong and how far apart stable tears must be to pair into a door, and how many a world holds.

cartography.label: Wild zones
cartography.explanation: How far a wild zone moves its ground and its cover between surveys.

cartography.label: Age of the world
cartography.explanation: How far the settled history runs before the present: hearths and chiefdoms, crowned realms, or lantern-lit cities. A longer age fills the land, gathers cities from their hinterlands and wears the ways into roads; the ice-age round before it stays.

cartography.label: Cultural pattern
cartography.explanation: Distinct concentrations or broader overlapping prevalence: how many identities begin and how far contact carries them. These fields do not prescribe political borders or simulate migration routes.

cartography.label: Political pattern
cartography.explanation: The scale and density of territorial partitions, independently of cultural prevalence: how many seats begin and how far each can hold.

cartography.label: Towns and cities
cartography.explanation: What settlement the map shows: many market towns, towns with a few cities drawing their hinterlands, or great cities gathering whole regions. Places below the World town size stay latent for finer maps.

cartography.label: Roads and travel
cartography.explanation: How readily use makes ways: tracks and fords between neighbours, roads worn between markets, or a realm's highways raised where its busiest roads cross open country.
